sentences.text:
Learned counsel for acquiring body has tendered copy of
judgment dated 12.12.2025, in First Appeal No. 257/2023, which is taken
on record and marked as exhibit 'X' for identification.
5.  The land of the appellants was acquired for Lendi Irrigation Project and notification under Section 4 was published on a Chawdi on 14.07.1999.
The award was passed by the SLAO and, thereafter, the Reference was made, which was registered as LAR No. 329/2011.

On 28.05.2019, Reference Court / Civil Judge, Senior Division, Mukhed, has partly allowed the Reference and has held that the respondent therein are jointly and severally are liable to pay enhanced compensation to the claimants for land bearing block no. 1/B to the extent of 35% more than what is decided by the LAO i.e. Rs. 04,01,417/- instead of Rs.
02,97,346/- to claimants as compensation.
The solatium and the additional component was also awarded apart from the interest.

6. Mr. Bagal, in order to cut short the controversy has submitted that since First Appeal No. 257/2023, was also pertaining to the land situated in the same village i.e. village Bhingoli, under the sane notification under Section 4 of Land Acquisition Act dated 14.07.1999,
and for the same project i.e. Lendi Irrigation Project, the same view be adopted.

8. I have gone through the judgment passed by this Court in First Appeal No. 257/2023, of which paragraph Nos. 8, 10 and 11 are as under :

sentences.text: 8. I have considered the rival submissions of the  parties.
The material  facts are undisputed.
The lands acquired in the present  appeals are from village Bhingoli.

For the self-same  project, when lands from Marajwadi were acquired, the  enhancement was granted by fixing rate of Rs.
 1,25,000/- per Hectare in First Appeal No. 834/2010  and connected matters.

The coordinate bench inter alia  relying upon the decisions rendered in First Appeal No.
 988/2012 and 989/2012, by a speaking order, the rate  was enhanced the rate.
The same formula of  enhancement has been applied by the coordinate bench  in the group of matters in First Appeal No. 3133/2009.
Lands in those matters are also from village  Marajwadi.
However, the coordinate bench marginally  deviated from the earlier formula by enhancing the  rate in the group of appeals decided on 02.05.2022 in  First Appeal No. 2036/2021 and connected matters.
The lands in those matters were from Bhaswadi and  acquired for the same project.
The enhancement of  compensation
was extended to 70% from that of the  4 919.odt reference Court, which is further followed in the common judgment passed on 31.07.2024 in First Appeal No. 1023/2022 and connected matter.
In the last couple of groups, this Court adopted the enhancement to 70% from the rate given by the reference Court, which is the latest formula.

I propose to adopt the same instead of enhancing the rate to Rs.
1,25,000/- per Hectare.
The enhancement to 70% is reasonable and adequate.
It is in consonance with the view taken by this Court.
11. The objection of the respondents is mainly on the distance and the location of the lands under acquisition as compared to the lands from Marajwadi and Bhaswadi.
The Cluster of village is affected because of Lendi project.

I have gone through a village map,
which shows that villages Bhingoli, Marajwadi and Bhaswadi are in the same vicinity.
The villages Bhaswadi and Marajwadi appear to be adjoining as against Bhingoli.

There is a distance between village Marajwadi and Bhingoli and that is the reason I am not inclined to accept enhancement of rate of Rs.
1,25,000/- per Hectare.
Ends of justice would be met by granting the enhancement to 70%."

sentences.text:
In paragraph nos. 8, 10 and 11, this Court has stated that since there is distance between village Marajwadi and Bhingoli, and therefore, the enhanced rate of compensation of Rs. 1,25,000/- cannot be made applicable to the land which was situated in village Bhingoli.
10.
Considering the aforesaid fact, 70% of the enhancement was granted.

Since the judgment passed in First Appeal No. 257/2023, dated 12.12.2025, has dealt with the aspect of enhancement of compensation at length and because the land of the claimants is also situated in village Bhingoli, under the same notification for the same purpose, I find that the same course can be adopted in the present matter.
Consequently, the appeal preferred by the claimants is also required to be allowed.

Accordingly, following order is passed :
 ORDER i. First Appeal is allowed partly.
ii. The compensation granted by the Reference Court shall stand enhanced to further 70%.
iii. Save and except above modification, rest of the award under challenge shall stand unaltered.
iv. Needless to state that interest shall be payable from the date of award.
6 919.odt v.
The appellant shall not be entitled to interest and statutory benefits for the delayed period, if there is any.
vi. The appellants shall pay the deficit Court fees.
vii. Award be drawn accordingly.
viii. Record and proceedings be sent back to the trial Court.

( RAJNISH R. VYAS, J. ) SPC Venkati Maroti Deokate And Ors vs The State Of Maharashtra And Ors on 4 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/185178702/
